Forecast Discussion

A front crosses the mountains today. It has no moisture to work with, so you notice only the breeze. Thursday and Friday are two mighty fine October days.

Hurricane Isaias makes landfall near Mobile, AL, Friday night and is over Jackson, TN, Sunday morning, weakening. The center never comes close to us. Most of our rain comes from the flow between that storm and a strong high off the Mid-Atlantic coast -- a river of Atlantic moisture driven into the east face of the Appalachians.

Rain develops from southwest to northeast Saturday, starting initially from the storm itself. The Atlantic flow takes over Saturday night, and that is when the rain turns heavier. Rain, heavy at times, continues into Sunday morning. Rain tapers Sunday afternoon. It's a lot of rain for the eastern edge of the Appalachians but less toward the west.

How fast the rain quits Sunday night is a point of uncertainty. The leftover energy from Isaias lingers overhead Monday with clouds and scattered showers, mainly in the western half of the Appalachians. Expect gusty winds Saturday night through Monday.

Tuesday is dry and mild. A front crosses Tuesday night but moisture is very limited. Wednesday is only slightly cooler but dry.
